One tunnel by default, IPv6 that is either on for real or off altogether, and a detector that checks what a name is really used on: its IPv6 node, its QUIC, a port it takes up later. A third-party code review went into this one as well.

To update, run the new `dpiswitch.exe` from anywhere and accept the offer to install over the installed version (one administrator prompt). Settings, lists, configs and verdicts are kept.

## Tunnels

- **The second tunnel is a switch in the settings, off by default.** Off, awg2 is not in the core's config and the UI says nothing of it; a `.conf` loaded for it is kept. An installation that had a second `.conf` keeps it switched on. Switching restarts the core, some 3 s.
- A second `.conf` with keys that are none, put there by hand, is left out instead of going into the config; the tunnels' pulse and the IPv6 uplink check go by the tunnels the config really has.
- A `.conf` is refused on an Endpoint port outside 1-65535 (70000 went in as 4464) and on an `AllowedIPs` entry that is no network.
- A tunnel resolver outside the tunnel's own address space is pinned alone, not with the whole /64 around it.

## IPv6

- **Off is no IPv6 at all.** Whatever learnt an IPv6 address past the core's DNS -- a browser's own DoH, an address dialled as it is -- used to leave by the physical adapter, around the tunnel and the rules. Off, the core's DNS gives no AAAA and a connection to an IPv6 address is refused.
- **On, a name's IPv6 node is checked beside its IPv4 one**, the cut and the QUIC decoy tried on it too: a name clean on IPv4 and cut on IPv6 went direct, and broke whenever the IPv6 node answered first. A node blocked by name is seen with no IPv6 in the tunnel as well; a node that does not take the connection, or is merely slower, does not count -- the core goes on with the IPv4 one. A lookup of the node that failed is asked once more before the node is given up.

## Detector and routes

- **A name going direct is checked on a port it is first seen on.** Found clean on tcp/443, a name went direct on every port and protocol, and its QUIC or a port a program took up later was never looked at: in three days of one machine's log, 89 such names had QUIC going direct unprobed.
- **The cut's names have their QUIC probed, seen on QUIC or not.** A name first met over TCP was never checked on QUIC again; on a network the decoy does not get through, its QUIC went nowhere unrefused.
- A page answered direct with another's certificate keeps its CDN family out of direct, as a blocked one does.
- A CDN's certificate is read only when it is the host's own -- chain, term and name checked: a node's default certificate, or one put in on the way, names no family.
- CDN families: undecided with fewer than 10 names checked, not the tunnel's way.
- Verdicts of names a list or a preset holds are set aside and put back, not dropped: a preset switched on and off again no longer costs YouTube its verdicts.
- The cut switched off closes everything its outbound carries, a family's and inheritance's connections too; families switched off, what their lists routed. The QUIC decoy switched off refuses QUIC on the ways the cut lends as well.
- The network is read off Windows' own tables, not off `route.exe` and `arp.exe`; an address Windows gives itself with no DHCP is no network.
- Memory: names dropped by hand stop waiting past their hour and go with a network dropped whole; a gateway's IPv6 finding follows it to its ISP; a reset empties the refusals too.

## UDP leak guard

- **The DHCP permit is the DHCP client's.** By the server's port alone it let any program's UDP to port 67 (547 over IPv6) of any address out around the tunnel -- checked against the Windows Filtering Platform: such a packet went through where others were dropped. It is from the client's port to the server's now.

## DNS cache

- An answer is one to the question asked; a question's key keeps its type as it is (HTTPS queries shared a key with another type).

## Service

- A failed write to the core's log -- a full disk -- no longer stops the reading of the core's output, which hung the core.
- deploy: the tray comes back when the administrator prompt is declined.

## Interface

- Live: speed in one column and bytes in one, columns that fill the window and can be dragged to a width, the date with the time, no sideways scroll.
- Tray: the UI's tab is found in any browser's window, Edge's with its tab count in the title.
- Presets that could not be read say so, in the page's language, and are not written over.
- Help and README: what was missing of the detector, and what was stale.

Core: the fork's 8067c742 (mihomo Alpha 9f053c49).
